coverage: Named roster: all eleven items reached. Fetched at the primary — Winterson (Guardian 12 Mar 2025), Kudan/Qudan (Japan Times 19 Jan 2024, quoting the acceptance speech), Mark Lawrence's two 2023 posts, Sudowrite Muse, Jane Friedman (7 Aug 2023), the Authors Guild survey release (15 May 2023, after the briefed URL 404'd), Clarke's 'A Concerning Trend' (15 Feb 2023, at neil-clarke.com; clarkesworldmagazine.com/clarke_02_23/ serves a different editorial), NPR (24 Feb 2023) and Hern's TechScape (which is dated 16 April 2024, not May). Recovered by ladder — Vara's 'Ghosts' via the Wayback raw capture (Believer live is Cloudflare-blocked); Doshi and Hauser via Europe PMC full-text XML (science.org Cloudflare-blocked); the DriveThruRPG storefront-filter page via Wayback. Not found at the primary — the July 2023 OneBookShelf written-content ban text: help.drivethrurpg.com is Cloudflare-blocked with no Wayback capture of that article, so it is recorded as a relay through EN World quoting Gizmodo, and the only primary DriveThru text reached (Oct 2024) labels artwork only, not AI-written text. Blocked and unread — the SSRN version of the Chakrabarty/Ginsburg/Dhillon paper (arXiv used instead, abstract only) and the Zenodo critique PDF (763-byte download). Expansion: bibliography chasing through the CHI 2026 paper's reference list yielded four further primaries (Art or Artifice, Can AI writing be salvaged, Readers Prefer Outputs of AI Trained on Copyrighted Books, Doshi and Hauser); arXiv API relevance queries yielded two more (the Chakrabarty/Dhillon paper itself and Farrell's Italian study); a lateral route through Simon Willison's link blog recovered the correct Guardian TechScape URL. 20 substantive sources of 22 read: 13 from the named roster and its policy relay, 5 by bibliography chasing through the CHI 2026 reference list, 2 by arXiv API relevance search; the two non-substantive rows are Simon Willison's link blog (used only to recover a URL) and the Zenodo critique whose PDF would not download. The WebSearch budget was exhausted mid-sweep, so the last expansion rounds used the arXiv, OpenAlex and Europe PMC APIs and reference-list chasing instead of open lateral search. Standing gap unchanged: no source read here measured the archival, encyclopedic or civic-record register — every measurement is on lyric poetry, flash or short fiction, literary excerpts of 450 words or less, or biomedical article vocabulary.
